title: 2-tile tall custom door reference keeps breaking

posts.author: castlemaniac
posts.body:
I am quite new to making assets & props for RPG maker games (specifically MV), the main problem is the doors and their customization. I try to make them a little taller than they usually are (48x48 tiles by default, however, the characters are 55x55, therefore it looks weird if they're just 1 tile tall), but the engine fails to capture the animation or illustration of the door without cutting awkwardly.
This is the door(s) intended animation loop / reference (it is 2 tiles tall, and 1 tile long):
Our tries to make it work (but did not worked):
We have tried to put terms like "
!
" or "
$
" in front of the file, or none at all, yet it only gives unfavorable results.
With an "$" first.
With an "!$" later.
With no special key in the asset's name.
Later, I tried I tried placing it instead in a 3x2 tile size just like the Gate1 asset (because it was 2 tiles tall), but it still did not worked.
(Original Gate1 image)
My attempt to replicate the same tile pattern:
And yet again, it did not worked.
For quite a while I believed that the prop should be yes or yes a 48x48 size, but again, it looks weird with the character:
The only thing I could find was this lovely tutorial for doors (
HERE
) made by Avery, and it made me realize that the doors can, in fact, be taller than the character's sprite. But I am unsure if for this I should change the tile's size from 48x48 to something taller (55x55 like the character's size), write an specific letter in the file's name, or simply stick with tiny doors.
I don't know either if there's a secret way of making this specific prop work with it's current height, but any help is truly appreciated. Please let me know if you need any extra details!

posts.author: Ahuramazda
posts.body:
I believe you had it correct with the name:
$office_door_test
but
, you are missing a 4th row of the door frame. Notice in the default version you linked as an example, it has a 4th row of the door 100% open... a sprite sheet is looking for a 3 wide, 4 tall layout.
If I am wrong on this someone else with more knowledge can correct me

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
$name = 4 rows, 3 column  (single sheet)
!$name = 4 rows, 3 column  (single sheet) but without offset +6 pixels up
name = 8 rows, 12 columns (like full actor sheet)
those are the base rules for sprites.
